parsed.title: Discussion on AI-assisted job search, development tools, and code generation pitfalls

topics.title: Using AI to automate job search and resume creation

claims.text: The author plans to set up an OpenClaw system to automatically find vacancies, generate PDFs of tailored resumes, and write cover letters.
Automation with AI is seen as beneficial because resumes attached to interviews are examined manually.
There is an expectation that AI skills such as Cursor, Claude Code, LLM, RAG, and embeddings will become essential for job seekers in 2026.
The author predicts that the recruiter profession will eventually become obsolete.
Using GPT to generate SQL joins and other code can speed up development, though it may produce suboptimal queries.
Despite speed gains, generated code can be insecure and inefficient, leading to long-running queries in production.
The speaker notes that their projects lack cloud infrastructure and unlikely to adopt it.

topics.title: Limitations of AI-generated code and developer context

claims.text: AI models cannot replace a developer's accumulated context, such as past decisions, workarounds, and domain knowledge.
Generated code may break projects and require manual review or full rollback.
Participants made jokes about AI controlling people and the evolution of attitudes toward AI between 2024 and 2026.
A humorous comparison of current tech stacks to REST, JSON, Microservices, Docker after React was made.
